one_line: Rudradaman I of the Western Kshatrapas and Vashishtiputra Satakarni of the Satavahanas, rival rulers bound by war and a diplomatic marriage alliance in 2nd‑century India.

appearance.age_look: Both appear in their late 30s to early 40s, athletic and battle-seasoned, with upright postures and broad shoulders.
appearance.face: Rudradaman has a strong oval face, wheatish complexion, straight sharp nose, neatly trimmed moustache and short boxed beard, with intense narrow eyes and a calm, calculating default gaze; Vashishtiputra has a slightly rounder face, medium-brown complexion, fuller moustache with a short neatly shaped beard, softer but steady eyes, and a composed, determined default expression.
appearance.hair: Rudradaman’s straight dark hair is shoulder-length, combed back and tied in a low knot at the back of the head, with a narrow silver diadem band resting above the forehead; Vashishtiputra’s dark wavy hair is gathered into a high side topknot (similar to early Satavahana reliefs) secured with a simple gold band and a small central pendant.
appearance.costume: Rudradaman wears a long-sleeved, thigh-length fitted tunic of fine off‑white cotton with a subtle vertical stripe weave, belted at the waist with a maroon cloth sash over a narrow leather belt; over this he has a light knee-length sleeveless coat in muted teal with a simple geometric border pattern in dark red and white along the edges, and close-fitting off‑white trousers tucked into mid-calf brown leather boots; his jewellery is restrained—two slim silver armlets, simple silver bangles, and a short silver necklace with a small central disc—reflecting Saka‑Iranian taste blended with local styles. Vashishtiputra wears a wrapped upper cloth (uttariya) of soft cream cotton, draped over both shoulders and crossing the chest, paired with a rich deep-ochre cotton dhoti wrapped tightly around the waist and falling to the ankles with neat pleats, secured by a broad dark-red cloth belt; over his torso he has a fitted sleeveless quilted vest in dull olive green, suggesting a padded armour style, with a narrow gold border and small round stitched motifs; he is barefoot or in simple dark leather sandals; his jewellery includes a broad gold torque necklace, a pair of plain gold earrings, and two gold armlets with subtle floral engraving, reflecting Satavahana court taste.
appearance.signature: Rudradaman carries a slightly curved single-edged steel sword with a plain crossguard and a brown leather-wrapped hilt in a simple brown scabbard slung from his belt, while Vashishtiputra carries a straight iron longsword with a rounded pommel and minimal guard, hanging from a cloth baldric crossing his chest.

ref_desc: Rudradaman has a shoulder-length tied-back dark hairstyle with a silver diadem, off-white tunic, teal sleeveless coat, off-white trousers and maroon sash with a curved sword, while Vashishtiputra has a high topknot with gold band, cream upper cloth, ochre dhoti, olive padded vest and a straight sword.
sheet_prompt: Draw two full-body anime-style male figures standing side by side as if for a historical character model sheet, clearly showing their faces, hair, clothing and weapons: first, Rudradaman, a late-30s athletic man with a strong oval face, wheatish complexion, moustache and short boxed beard, intense narrow eyes and a calm, calculating expression; his straight dark hair reaches the shoulders, combed back and tied in a low knot, with a narrow silver diadem band above his forehead; he wears a long-sleeved, thigh-length fitted off-white cotton tunic with subtle vertical stripes, belted with a deep maroon cloth sash over a narrow leather belt, a light knee-length sleeveless coat in muted teal with simple dark red and white geometric border patterns, close-fitting off-white trousers, and brown mid-calf leather boots, with minimal silver jewellery (slim armlets, bangles and a short disc necklace); at his side hangs a slightly curved single-edged steel sword with a plain crossguard and brown leather-wrapped hilt in a simple brown scabbard. Next to him, Vashishtiputra Satakarni, also late-30s, athletic with a slightly rounder medium-brown face, full moustache and short neatly shaped beard, steady eyes and a composed determined expression; his dark wavy hair is gathered into a high side topknot secured with a simple gold band and a small central pendant; he wears a cream cotton upper cloth wrapped over both shoulders and across the chest, a deep-ochre ankle-length dhoti with neat pleats held by a broad dark-red cloth belt, and a fitted sleeveless quilted vest in dull olive green with a narrow gold border and small round stitched motifs, along with a broad gold torque, plain gold earrings and gold armlets; he stands barefoot or in simple dark leather sandals, with a straight iron longsword with rounded pommel and minimal guard hanging from a cloth baldric across his chest; use a restrained palette of off-white, deep maroon, muted teal, deep ochre and olive green, keeping all garments modest, historically grounded for 2nd-century Western Deccan and Aparanta, and avoiding any fantasy elements.
